thread:
jess: FYI customer on private deployment (no-internet mode) reporting intermittent API failures when calling Redwood endpoints from their on-prem inference gateway. They see TLS handshake failures and 502s. Happening since yesterday after a proxy upgrade.
liam: Can you paste the exact error and a minimal repro command?
jess: Repro with curl from their gateway: 
```
curl -v -x http://proxy.corp:3128 https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health
*   Trying 10.0.0.5:3128... connected
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Certificate (11)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Finished (20)
* SSL connection using TLSv1.2 / ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384
* Server certificate: redwood.internal
* Server certificate subject: CN=redwood.internal
> GET /v1/health HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example.com
> User-Agent: curl/7.61.1
> Accept: */*
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< Content-Type: text/html
<
{ "error": "upstream TLS mismatch" }
```
They also see TLS_alert 40 in sni logs.
prateek: Looks like proxy is terminating TLS and presenting its own cert (redwood.internal) rather than passing through SNI. In no-internet mode they should be using CONNECT passthrough for TLS to Redwood, not TLS-terminating. Can we get a tcpdump of the 443 flow and an openssl s_client capture?
maria: Also check DNS: if the gateway resolves api.redwood.example.com to an internal proxy IP that then rewraps traffic, SNI could be rewritten. Can you run `dig +short api.redwood.example.com` and `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example.com:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com -showcerts` from gateway?
jess: Customer ran commands, pasted outputs: 
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.example.com
10.0.10.11\n\n$ openssl s_client -connect 10.0.10.11:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)\ndepth=0 CN = redwood.internal\nverify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate\n---\n2500 server problems, 0 OK\n```
They say the proxy is doing SSL bridging and presenting internal certs.
liam: That matches. Two likely roots: 1) proxy intentionally inspects TLS and reissues certs (MITM) — needs to be configured to forward SNI and allow CONNECT for our endpoints; 2) egress firewall rewrites/dest-NAT to an internal terminator that doesn't forward original SNI.
prateek: Additional check: see if CONNECT method is being used by the client. When using an HTTP proxy, `curl -v` should show `Proxy CONNECT` vs regular `GET`. If proxy is responding to CONNECT with 200 then doing its own TLS handshake, it's TLS-inspecting. Example command: `curl -x http://proxy:3128 -vvv --proxy-insecure https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health`.
maria: For short-term workaround, we recommend: - Configure proxy to allow CONNECT passthrough for api.redwood.example.com (and our control-plane hostnames). - If TLS inspection is required, ensure the proxy is configured to SNI-preserve and the reissued certs include SAN for api.redwood.example.com, or add host exceptions to route directly to Redwood egress IPs.
jess: Customer also ran `tcpdump -n -A port 443` and we see `ClientHello` with SNI=api.redwood.example.com, but server returns a cert for redwood.internal — so proxy is MITM. They can't disable inspection globally for compliance, so they want specific allowlist for Redwood to be passthrough.
liam: We'll need to provide the IP ranges/domains to allow-direct. Ask them to allow outbound to our control plane and data-plane: domains: `*.redwood.sh`, `api.redwood.example.com`, and IPs: 34.210.45.10, 34.210.45.11, 3.120.200.77 (these are example IPs — will confirm with infra).
prateek: Also check proxy auth: if proxy requires NTLM/Kerberos, some clients will downgrade CONNECT semantics. Confirm curl used `--proxy-user` or proper auth.
maria: Can you also check if the proxy rewrites Host header? In some devices the Host header is replaced which can break virtual-hosted TLS routers behind NAT. `tcpdump` showing ClientHello SNI but Host header replaced would point to a different middlebox.
jess: Customer can't add direct allowlist right away. They asked if we can provide a debug build to accept the proxy-reissued cert as a trusted CA for a short test (they control the proxy CA). I told them our SDKs support custom trust stores in Private deployments but we'd need a support bundle and policy signoff.
eng-oncall: Escalating to eng-runtime: can we confirm the canonical egress IPs and whether we can support a cert-pinning bypass for private customers in no-internet mode? Also need to check if our control plane traffic uses SNI for routing — we should document exact FQDNs to allow.
support-bot: Created INC-4729 and linked to case #SUP-9982.
jess: Customer provided support bundle and proxy config snippets (PAC): 
```
function FindProxyForURL(url, host) {
  if (shExpMatch(host, "*.redwood.sh") || host == "api.redwood.example.com") return "DIRECT";
  return "PROXY proxy.corp:3128";
}
```
They deployed this and initial tests succeeded (health endpoint returns 200) but long-running streaming calls later dropped with 504s.
liam: That sounds like a long-lived connection NAT timeout or conntrack exhaustion on the proxy/gateway. Ask them to check idle timeouts and conntrack table size. Also check proxy's Keep-Alive and buffering for streaming endpoints.
prateek: Repro steps for them to run and attach: 1) `curl --http1.1 -v -x http://proxy:3128 https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/stream --header "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"` 2) `ss -s` or `netstat -an | grep 443 | wc -l` on gateway during stream 3) `sudo conntrack -L | grep 10.0.10.11` (if conntrack available).
maria: I'll draft a KB we can share: minimal allowlist + PAC snippet + common proxy gotchas (SNI MITM, NTLM dance, CONNECT timeouts, keepalives). jess, once you confirm the IP ranges from infra I'll add to the KB and close the loop.
jess: Customer will try PAC + adjust conntrack/keepalive and report back tomorrow. Adding all participants. Thanks. :thumbsup:
